subject: Franska
title: Articles and gender
sourceSummary: Definite and indefinite articles, gender (masculine/feminine), and the plural of nouns.

questions.prompt: How many genders do French nouns have?
questions.explanation: French has two genders: masculine (le) and feminine (la). There is no neuter.

questions.prompt: Choose the right article: "___ maison est grande." (The house is big.)
questions.opener: "Maison" is feminine — and also starts with a consonant.
questions.explanation: "Maison" (house) is feminine singular, so the article is "la". "Le" is used for masculine words, "les" is plural.

questions.prompt: Choose the right article: "___ école est loin." (The school is far away.)
questions.explanation: In front of words starting with a vowel sound, both "le" and "la" shorten to "l'": "l'école". The gender (feminine) is no longer visible on the article, but it still affects things like adjectives later on.

questions.prompt: Choose the right article: "Je veux acheter ___ pomme." (I want to buy an apple.)
questions.explanation: "Une" is the indefinite article for feminine ("a/an"). "Un" is masculine, and "des" means "some".

questions.prompt: What is the plural of "le livre" (the book)?
questions.opener: Most French nouns form the plural with -s, which is often NOT pronounced.
questions.explanation: The plural is formed with -s: "livre" → "livres", and the article becomes "les" (the plural article for both genders). Note that -s is usually not heard when speaking.

questions.prompt: Write the plural of "la table" (the table) — just the word for "table", not the article.
Correct the two errors: "Le table est nouvelle et j'ai un pomme rouge."
questions.opener: Check the gender of "table" and "pomme" — both are feminine.
questions.answer: La table est nouvelle et j'ai une pomme rouge.
steps: "Le table" → "La table". "Table" is feminine, so the article should be "la", not "le".
"Un pomme" → "une pomme". "Pomme" (apple) is also feminine, so it should be "une", not "un".
Gender has to be learned with each word — it's rarely possible to guess it from the meaning.

questions.prompt: How do gender, definite/indefinite articles, and plural work in French?
questions.opener: Two genders, and how the articles follow along.
questions.answer: Gender: le (masculine, e.g. le livre), la (feminine, e.g. la table) — must be learned with each word. Before a vowel sound: both le and la become l' (l'école, l'ami). Definite article plural: les (same for both genders). Indefinite article: un (masc.), une (fem.), des (plural, 'some'). Plural: almost always noun + -s (usually not pronounced), with the article les.

questions.prompt: Choose the right article: "___ voiture est rouge." (The car is red.)
questions.opener: "Voiture" is feminine and starts with a consonant.
questions.explanation: "Voiture" (car) is feminine singular and starts with a consonant, so the article is "la".

questions.prompt: Choose the right article: "J'ai ___ chien." (I have a dog.)
questions.explanation: "Un" is the indefinite article for masculine. "Une" is used instead for feminine.

questions.prompt: What is the plural of "le cheval" (the horse)?
questions.opener: An irregular pattern: words ending in -al often switch to -aux in the plural.
questions.explanation: "Cheval" → "chevaux" in the plural (the irregular -al → -aux ending), with the article "les".

questions.prompt: What gender is the word "la lune" (the moon)?
questions.opener: The article "la" gives away the gender directly.
questions.explanation: "La lune" takes the article "la", which means the word is feminine.

questions.prompt: Choose the right article: "___ ami s'appelle Marc." (The friend's name is Marc.)
questions.opener: "Ami" is masculine but starts with a vowel.
questions.explanation: In front of words starting with a vowel sound, "le" shortens to "l'": "l'ami".

questions.prompt: What is the plural of "la fleur" (the flower)?
questions.opener: "Fleur" forms the plural with the regular -s pattern.
questions.explanation: "Fleur" → "fleurs" in the plural, with the article "les".

questions.prompt: What gender is the word "le soleil" (the sun)?
questions.opener: The article "le" gives away the gender directly.
questions.explanation: "Le soleil" takes the article "le", which means the word is masculine.
